key_insight: Omni123 unifies text-to-2D and text-to-3D generation so a single 3D-native foundation model can learn strong, geometry-consistent 3D synthesis by leveraging abundant 2D data together with limited 3D assets.
problem_solved: Addresses the scarcity of high-quality 3D training data and the geometric inconsistency of prior pipelines that rely on editing in 2D then lifting to 3D via optimization.
method: Train a shared multimodal backbone with separate 2D and 3D heads so text supervision can improve both image and 3D generation.

Combine large-scale 2D image-caption pairs with a small curated 3D dataset using cross-task consistency losses, differentiable rendering / multi-view supervision, and geometric regularizers to provide pseudo-3D signals from 2D data.

Design a 3D-native generative decoder (view-conditioned neural renderer / NeRF-style latent) that enforces multi-view coherence and aligns rendered 2D outputs with the 2D generation head via contrastive or reconstruction losses.
impact: Enables data-efficient training of geometry-faithful 3D generative models without relying on large 3D repositories, accelerating AR/VR content creation, robotics simulation, and downstream multimodal research.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: text → shared backbone → parallel 2D head and 3D-native head (with differentiable renderer and consistency losses annotated)
Data-efficiency bar chart: performance vs. amount of 3D data (Omni123 vs baselines) showing gains from using 2D data
Multi-view qualitative grid: generated object from multiple camera angles demonstrating geometric consistency
Loss/consistency schematic: arrows showing cross-modal alignment (text↔2D, 2D↔rendered 3D, multi-view constraints)
paper_title: Omni123: Exploring 3D Native Foundation Models with Limited 3D Data by Unifying Text to 2D and 3D Generation
paper_authors: Chongjie Ye, Cheng Cao, Chuanyu Pan, Yiming Hao, Yihao Zhi
